summary: Reviewed apps/web/e2e/* against AGENTS.md, apps/web/README.md, apps/web/e2e/README.md, docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/WORK-ORDER.md and RIG.md, .claude/skills/tdd/SKILL.md + tests.md + mocking.md, and the Fowler smell baseline. packages/db and packages/runtime are untouched by this diff, so their READMEs carry no findings. The three commits are genuine vertical slices (test + implementation together in each commit; git log --stat shows no horizontal red-battery commit), every commit carries the required Co-Authored-By line and names its ticket, apps/web/e2e/README.md was updated in the same commits as the code it documents, apps/web/test/manifest.txt's two new lines sit at the correct sorted position (shared-file rule 7 honoured), CONTEXT.md was correctly left untouched (no new domain vocabulary), and the sign-in-census.test.ts / run-args.test.ts structural-census cells are exactly the kind of 'catalog census' this repo's own TDD override sanctions -- not flagged as a /tdd seam violation despite reading file source instead of a public runtime interface. Two verified, reproducible defects survive that reading, both centered on #851's two new files: (1) both new .test.ts files are unintentionally live Playwright specs because playwright.config.ts never narrows Playwright's stock testMatch away from Node-runner files, which means a failing census assertion silently flips the exit code of the documented bare `pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e` command even when every browser test is green; and (2) the census's own core detector has an asymmetric blind spot that lets a trivially-reshaped local sign-in evade it entirely, undermining the guarantee AC2 claims. Both were verified by direct reproduction in this checkout (commands and output below), not inferred. Neither blocks the two tickets' stated acceptance criteria from being true today (no current spec file happens to trip either gap), so verdict is accept-with-fixes rather than reject.

findings.title: run-args.test.ts and sign-in-census.test.ts are unintentionally live Playwright specs; a failing census assertion silently corrupts a green bare e2e run's exit code
findings.evidence: apps/web/playwright.config.ts sets testDir: "./e2e" and never overrides `testMatch`, so Playwright's own stock default applies -- confirmed by reading node_modules/.pnpm/playwright@1.62.1/node_modules/playwright/lib/common/index.js:639: `testMatch: takeFirst(projectConfig.testMatch, config.testMatch, "**/*.@(spec|test).?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)")` -- which matches `*.test.ts` as well as `*.spec.ts`. Reproduced live in this checkout: `pnpm --filter @clara/web exec playwright test --list` (no spec filter, i.e. the shape of the documented bare `pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e` command in apps/web/e2e/README.md's very first code block) requires every matching file under e2e/, and its stdout shows raw TAP output from `node:test` interleaved with Playwright's own listing -- `TAP version 13` followed by `ok 27 - #851 · a bare run is byte-for-byte...` through `ok 35 - #851 · THE VACUITY CONTROL...`, i.e. all nine assertions from this PR's two new files ran as an uncontrolled side effect of Playwright's file loader `import`-ing them, alongside the two pre-existing e2e/*.test.ts files' own TAP output. A minimal, isolated repro (two throwaway files in the scratchpad, not in the repo) confirms the consequence: a host script that merely `import()`s a node:test file containing one failing `assert.equal` sees `process.exitCode` still `undefined` immediately after the synchronous import returns, but the real process exit code is 1 once the event loop drains -- i.e. the exact mechanism by which Playwright's own process would inherit a failed census assertion's exit code even though Playwright itself never ran or reported that test. A targeted run (`playwright test --list documents-viewer-walk`) does NOT exhibit this, because Playwright applies the CLI path-filter before requiring files -- which is also why none of wave1-lane02-final.md's browser-walk gate evidence (every command passes an explicit spec-name filter) could have caught this: the lane never ran the bare, filterless command the README documents as the suite's primary entry point.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit `testMatch` (e.g. `/.*\.spec\.ts$/`) or `testIgnore` for `*.test.ts` to apps/web/playwright.config.ts so Playwright's file discovery only ever sees `*.spec.ts`, closing the leak for both files this PR adds and the two pre-existing ones (e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, e2e/mock-dispatch.test.ts).

findings.title: The sign-in census's own form detector has an asymmetric indirection blind spot: a trivially reshaped local sign-in evades reimplementsLoginForm() entirely
findings.evidence: apps/web/e2e/sign-in-census.test.ts's `SIGN_IN_SUBMIT` regex is deliberately written to catch an indirected button locator (its own comment: 'THE BUTTON HALF IS A REFERENCE, NOT A `.click()`, deliberately... the shape a real offender takes just as easily -- `const button = page.getByRole(...); await button.click();`'), and the file's vacuity-control test proves this works for the button half. But the sibling `PASSWORD_FILL` regex (`/getByLabel\(\s*(?:(["'])Password\1|\/[^/\n]*password[^/\n]*\/[a-z]*)\s*\)\s*\.fill\(/i`) requires `.fill(` to chain directly onto `getByLabel(...)` with no equivalent indirection handling. Verified by direct evaluation of both regexes (extracted byte-for-byte from the file) against: `const password = page.getByLabel("Password"); await password.fill("Clara-e2e-password-1!"); const submit = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }); await submit.click();` -- `PASSWORD_FILL.test(src)` returns `false`, `SIGN_IN_SUBMIT.test(src)` returns `true`, and `reimplementsLoginForm()` therefore returns `false` for a source string that unambiguously drives the login form with the exact fixture password and the exact submit button, using the SAME 'assign locator to a variable first' style the file already treats as the discriminating case for the button. No cell in the file's own 'VACUITY CONTROL' test exercises an indirected Password locator, so this gap was not caught by the PR's own tests. Because the file's stated purpose is reading the form 'rather than a function name... so a local helper called anything at all is caught,' and AC2 of #851 is 'A census cell fails when a spec file defines its own local sign-in... the census cell proves it,' this is the /tdd anti-pattern of a test that would still pass (stay green) against a reintroduced, functionally-identical instance of the exact defect it exists to catch.
findings.required_fix: Generalize `PASSWORD_FILL` the same way `SIGN_IN_SUBMIT` already is -- match a `getByLabel("Password"|/password/i)` call anywhere in the source combined with a `.fill(` call reachable from it (or, simplest, drop the requirement that `.fill(` chain directly and instead require the two to co-occur alongside a `.fill(` call anywhere in the file, mirroring the button's own looser reference-based match) -- and add a vacuity-control case for the indirected-password shape so the fix is pinned.

findings.title: Possible Primitive Obsession: a one-element array stands in for a captured-once Maybe value
findings.evidence: apps/web/e2e/documents-viewer-walk.spec.ts: `const resized: OverlayWidths[] = [];` is pushed to at most once inside the poll callback and then read as `resized[0]!`, with `expect(resized).toHaveLength(1)` standing in for a null/undefined check. A `let captured: OverlayWidths | null = null` with `expect(captured).not.toBeNull()` would say the same thing without an array standing in for an optional single value. This is a labelled judgement call, not a hard violation: the shape is deliberate and the accompanying comment argues for it directly ('The capture is itself asserted... which is the vacuous shape this edit exists to remove'), and the choice does not weaken the assertion it replaces.
findings.required_fix: Optional: consider a nullable variable instead of a single-slot array, for a reader who has not seen the comment; not required given the existing justification.
